items.title: Mayor's Inaugural Address
notes: Mayor Watters welcomed all to our Council Chamber for this Inaugural Council Meeting and further welcomed those of you watching from home. He continued with the following:
“I would like to acknowledge the support of my friends and family and especially my wife Deb, whose love and guidance has made me a better person. I love you Deb.

I want to recognize Mayor Linton and thank the 2018 to 2021 Council for their dedicated service. I would also like to thank staff for their continued support and professionalism as we make the transition to this new Council. Centre Wellington is a better place because of your contribution and efforts.

My congratulations to all of you that are now sitting around this horseshoe. I am immensely proud of your past community involvement and so pleased you have found your way to be newly elected members of this constituted Council. Your families and friends I am sure are equally proud of you. I thank you for putting yourself out there. At times you will be scrutinized by the public and it may get tough, however, you will get through these times because of the support you have around you, especially as we support one another as a team. Remember you are not an island.

These are challenging times, and they will test our mettle as a Council as we move forward. Mutual respect, listening to one another and being supportive of each other are keys to building a team that will be able to meet these challenges.

I also ask the public to be patient as the new council settles in and develops a good understanding of our new roles and responsibilities. As we move forward as a Council, our challenges will include some of the following:
- Managing our growth targets and working towards an attainable housing strategy;
- Planning a sustainable, healthy and livable community;
- Providing a cost-effective Infrastructure which is timely and highlights our roads and bridge network;
- Developing a Short-term rentals strategy;
- Managing our financial budgets which is mindful of these challenging times.
Developing a parking strategy for our downtown area.
- Protection of our water and farmland resources.
- Developing a climate adaptation strategy.
- Preserving our architecture, cultural heritage, and natural landscapes.
- Building a welcoming and inclusive community.
- Developing a respectful and accountable council.

For Council to meet these challenges, we must support each other as we work with committees, staff, and the public. Finally, our relationships with First Nations, County of Wellington and the Province are also extremely important as we are partners and thus our mutual respect and our ability to work through issues is of high importance and should be a common goal.

Centre Wellington can be a leader in rural community development if we are not afraid to speak out and are willing to listen and work towards sustainable solutions with our partners and the public. Lastly, Councillors, Relax! Smile! This is your night and please enjoy. Good evening to you all. Meeting Adjourn. Be proud!”

items.title: Mayor Watters called the meeting adjourned.
